subject: [hw] V40 -> D01: ten facts for FACTS.md (VCU ABI layout, log/mmap-type ioctls, GCE/cache semantics)
body:
Facts from V40 for FACTS.md (all [V] from the kernel source unless marked; add or reject as you see fit). Evidence command for the layout rows: clang --target=armv7a-linux-gnueabi -c -I <K>/include/uapi gpu/hwcodec/vcu/test_v40/layout_probe.c, table read from the .probe section (59 words, run by vcu/test_v40/run_tests.sh).

1. struct gce_cmds (the VCU_GCE_SET_CMD_FLUSH command list) is 0xe808 bytes for a 32-bit AAPCS daemon, with cmd at 0, addr at 0x800, data at 0x4800, mask at 0x8800, dma_offset at 0xa800, dma_size at 0xc800, cmd_cnt at 0xe800. The u64 arrays are 8-byte aligned under AAPCS, which is what makes it 0xe808 and not 0xe804. Evidence: mtk_vcu_controls.h:54-62 compiled for armv7a; V40 layout_probe.c table words 9-16. [V]

2. VCU_SET_LOG_OBJECT is `_IOW('v',12,struct log_test)` and `struct log_test` is defined nowhere in this kernel tree (grep of drivers/, include/, uapi/ finds only the macro and log_test_nofuse), so its request number cannot be derived from source: the size field is unknowable. The daemon never sends it (D01 s vcu_usage.md has no such literal). V40 accepts nr 12 with any _IOC size. Evidence: mtk_vcu_controls.h:189,225; grep -rn "struct log_test" over nord2-current-kernel. [V]

3. VCU_SET_MMAP_TYPE (nr 13, struct map_obj) is NOT handled by mtk_vcu_unlocked_ioctl: there is no case for it in the switch, so it reaches `default: dev_err("Unknown cmd")` and returns ret = -1 (EPERM to user space). It is also never sent by the vendor set (no literal in D01 s scan). V40 accepts it and returns 0, documented as a deviation. Evidence: mtk_vcu.c:1789-1972 (no case 13), :1966-1968. [V]

4. The VCU DMEM is allocated unconditionally at probe time with VCU_SHMEM_SIZE = 0x80000 (not lazily on vdec init), so a MAP_SHMEM_ALLOC/COMMIT mmap always has a backing buffer on the phone. Evidence: mtk_vcu.c:94, :1596-1619, :2542. [V]

5. VCU_GCE_SET_CMD_FLUSH with cmd_cnt >= VCODEC_CMDQ_CMD_MAX (2048) clamps cmd_cnt to 2048, sets ret = -EINVAL but still builds and flushes the (clamped) list, so the ioctl returns -EINVAL although all 2048 commands were executed. Exactly 2048 is already "overflow". Evidence: mtk_vcu.c:1036-1041, the loop at :1060-1080, return at :1094. [V]

6. Cache maintenance through /dev/vcu only sees vb2 (VCU_MVA_ALLOCATION) buffers: vcu_buffer_cache_sync walks vcu_queue->bufs and returns -1 (EINVAL) when the range matches none, and vcu_buffer_flush_all skips the PA page list. A VCU_CACHE_FLUSH_BUFF/INVALIDATE_BUFF on a VCU_PA_ALLOCATION page therefore fails with EINVAL. Evidence: mtk_vcodec_mem.c:358-392, :394-430; mtk_vcu.c:1927-1958. [V]

7. vcu_check_gce_pa_base() accepts only an address inside the FIRST PAGE of a PA allocation (`addr + length <= tmp->pa + PAGE_SIZE`), independent of the allocation length; CMD_MEM_MV and CMD_POLL_ADDR on memory are therefore single-page by construction, which is what cmdq_mbox_buf_alloc returns. Evidence: mtk_vcu.c:632-650, :752-788. [V]

8. VCU_SET_OBJECT does not validate share_obj.len: it copies sizeof(share_obj) from user, checks only `id` (IPI_VCU_INIT <= id < IPI_MAX), then calls the handler with (share_buf, len, priv) and copies the object back, returning copy_to_user s result (0) even when vcu_ipi_handler returned -1 for an unregistered id. V40 clamps len to 80 before the handler (deviation, memory safety). Evidence: mtk_vcu.c:1805-1823, :1396-1420. [V]

9. The mmap decision order of mtk_vcu_mmap is: (a) if the previous VCU_PA_ALLOCATION set map_buf_pa (pa + 0x800000000), the offset is treated as a physical address and looked up in the PA page list; (b) offset < 0x40000000 goes through vcu_check_reg_base() against the three VCU windows; (c) MAP_SHMEM_ALLOC [0x80000000,0x80080000] and COMMIT [0x88000000,0x88080000] map the DMEM, always from its start (the offset inside the range is ignored); (d) MM/CACHEABLE/PA bases map an iova/pa. V40 reproduces (a)-(d) and honours the in-range DMEM offset (deviation). Evidence: mtk_vcu.c:1653-1795, :1871-1873, :100-113. [V]

10. ipi_id_to_inst_id() maps ids 0..13 (IPI_VCU_INIT..IPI_VDEC_AV1) to the VDEC slot and 14..49 (IPI_VENC_COMMON..) to the VENC slot, including out-of-range/garbage ids (they go to VENC). One user_obj per slot, so two outstanding AP->daemon messages on different VENC ids overwrite each other. Evidence: mtk_vcu.c:118-125, :421-426. [V]
